goal: Stop a wedged postgres.js pool connection (active+ClientRead socket stall) from poisoning the worker pool: bulkhead HealthAlertPoller onto its own dedicated client that self-heals by destroy+rebuild on withTimeout expiry, and add a slow-cadence PoolWedgeReaperPoller that pg_terminate_backends the wedge signature (active+ClientRead, state_change age > threshold, RepWorth-owned-table query fingerprint) on a dedicated pooler-bypassing connection.
non_goals: Reproducing or eliminating the root-cause driver/socket stall itself — the trigger is a rare stall; the bisect (#490 concurrency, Supavisor server-slots) is opportunistic/time-boxed only, and the fix heals regardless of trigger.
Implementing #477's worker-vs-dashboard pool split or pool-wait observability (separate ticket, blocked by #474). The reaper's dedicated client is wedge-containment, not the pool split.
Moving the whole worker off the Supavisor transaction pooler onto direct/session-mode connections.
Changing any health-check SQL, thresholds, or semantics.
Per-query cancellation via postgres.js .cancel() — rejected: unproven against a socket wedge; client-side destroy+rebuild is the chosen reclaim.
Any change to approval / auto-approval / billing / moderation logic.
user_visible_behavior: A wedged health-check connection self-heals within one poll cycle (<=~30s) instead of permanently starving the pool.
HealthAlertPoller's wedge no longer starves the shared pool / the other ~20 loops — it is bulkheaded onto its own dedicated client.
New PoolWedgeReaperPoller terminates any RepWorth-owned backend stuck in active+ClientRead beyond the age threshold, emitting a warning-level structured log (and health finding) on each termination.
When the worker has no DATABASE_URL, the reaper logs once and stays disabled — no crash, no fallback onto the pooler it is meant to heal.
On ticket close, the HEALTH_ALERT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=86400000 staging mitigation is reverted to the 300000 default.
invariants: The reaper NEVER terminates a backend unless it is BOTH pathologically stuck (active AND wait_event='ClientRead' AND now()-state_change > threshold) AND running a query against a RepWorth-owned table (job_outbox/flagged_responses/responses/notification_deliveries) — so it can never kill another Supavisor client's backend.
A per-sweep termination cap (runaway guard) is never exceeded; when candidates exceed the cap the dropped count is logged.
Best-effort/observability failures in the reaper or the health-client recycle never crash the worker nor flip a completed job to failed (production.md log-and-swallow; crash-net stays intact).
Health checks remain read-only; the reaper's pg_terminate_backend is the only new server-side side effect and runs solely on the reaper's own dedicated connection.
Invariant #15: dedicated postgres clients are created only via the src/lib/db/server owner factory and used only by composition-root pollers registered in worker/index.ts.
The reaper runs on a connection that BYPASSES the (possibly-saturated) transaction pooler (DATABASE_URL, session mode), so it can heal even during a full-pool outage.
No change to approval/auto-approval/billing/moderation paths; tenant-scope and RLS audits stay green.
edge_cases: Supavisor flattens client application_name to 'Supavisor' server-side -> backend identity must use query fingerprint, not app_name (captured as ADR 0007).
query_start may restamp each cycle -> the age filter keys on state_change (continuously-stuck-active), not query_start.
Multiple wedged backends in one sweep -> apply the cap, terminate oldest-first (by state_change), log the count dropped by the cap.
DATABASE_URL absent on the worker -> reaper disabled + logged once (fail-safe), never crashed, never pooler-fallback.
healthSql.end() on a wedged connection must force-close within a short timeout because the query never settles -> end({ timeout: small }) then rebuild a fresh client.
The reaper's own dedicated (direct) connection may fail to connect -> log, skip the cycle, retry next cadence; no crash.
pg_terminate_backend returns false if the pid already vanished (self-heal/redeploy race) -> tolerate.
Reaper fingerprint may also match the now-bulkheaded health poller's own wedge; self-heal should win first, but an overlapping terminate is harmless (both kill the same stuck backend).
